thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PAGED: PrivateConnect customer connectivity degradation (customer: AcmeCorp) — possible split routing + DNS bounce in metro pair eastus3. See below for details and runbook links. Please ack.

alex: acked. I’m on call. Pulling BGP tables and prefix origin now.

maya: I’m seeing customer reports of intermittent DNS failures and TCP resets to their PrivateLink endpoint. They say it started ~12:05 UTC.

alex: timeline from infra metrics: spike in 5xxs for privatelink-proxy-eastus3b at 12:06, CPU normal but packet drop counters increasing on SGW.

sam-netops: running basic traceroute from our edge to their endpoint — we see two different next-hops alternating between az-a and az-b in the metro. Looks like route oscillation.

alex: posting traceroute output:```traceroute to 10.120.55.23 (10.120.55.23), 30 hops max, 60 byte packets
 1  10.10.0.1  0.8 ms  0.7 ms  0.7 ms
 2  100.64.1.5  1.2 ms  1.1 ms  1.1 ms
 3  192.0.2.17  3.9 ms  4.0 ms  3.8 ms
 4  198.51.100.9  6.8 ms  6.7 ms  6.9 ms
 5  10.120.55.23  9.2 ms  8.9 ms  9.0 ms
```

maya: I also grabbed BGP show for the prefix — two peers advertising same prefix with different AS-PATH length and occasionally withdraw then re-advertise. looks like a metro-level path flap.

alex: paste of BGP snippet:```BGP> show ip bgp 203.0.113.0/24
Paths: (2 available, best #2, table default)
  Not advertised to any peer
  65001 65010  192.0.2.0 from 198.51.100.1
    Origin IGP, localpref 100, valid, external
  65001 65020  192.0.2.0 from 198.51.100.2
    Origin IGP, localpref 100, valid, external
```

tj-oncall: @sam-netops can you check route-reflector logs for any flapping? Also any recent config pushes to peering devices?

sam-netops: looking — no config pushes in last 4 hours. RR logs show withdraw/announce cycles for that prefix around 12:05–12:12. Possible partner-side flapping or internal multipath race.

eva-eng: customer CS reports DNS queries to privatelink endpoint returning NXDOMAIN intermittently — could be that the endpoint fronting VIP is bouncing between AZs and the DNS resolver cache TTL is short.

alex: quick mitigation idea: apply temporary inbound geo/az stickiness on the proxy LB for AcmeCorp prefixes (force consistent AZ path) and add a short-term BGP dampening on the flapping path. Need approval.

maya: thumbs up from me. Risk: dampening could suppress legitimate failover. Keep conservative timers and monitor.

tj-oncall: agree. Do a targeted dampening on the specific neighbor (198.51.100.2) with half-life 300s, reuse 8000, suppress 20000 — conservative. Also pin load-balancer session affinity for that customer for 30m.

sam-netops: executing now. Commands:```configure terminal
router bgp 65001
 neighbor 198.51.100.2 route-map DAMP-IN in
route-map DAMP-IN permit 10
 set dampening 8000 300 20000 300
exit
```Applying route-map on RR.

incident-bot: Action logged: dampening rule applied to neighbor 198.51.100.2 by sam-netops at 12:18 UTC. LB sticky session policy applied to privatelink-proxy-eastus3 for prefix 203.0.113.0/24.

maya: after change I’m seeing fewer withdraws — last 10m looks stable. Customer 5xxs down from ~18% to ~1.5% in metrics.

customer-success: pinged AcmeCorp and told them we applied mitigations and will monitor. They asked for ETA for full fix and impact window.

alex: short-term mitigation looks effective. We need root cause: partner AS (65020) is flapping — setting up bridge with partner NOC and scheduling a postmortem. Also we should prepare a PR to our fallback policy to prefer the non-flapping peer during instability.

eva-eng: creating an incident ticket and assigning Sev2. Adding links to runbook and the action items.

tj-oncall: handing off to @maya for next shift — I have to step out in 20. Please keep monitoring for 2 hours and escalate if reoccurs.

maya: taking handoff. I’ll keep a watch on BGP state and customer error rate. Setting reminders to lift dampening after 2 hours if stable.

alex: final notes for now: mitigation applied, customer impact reduced to minor; partner NOC engaged; follow-up action items: (1) coordinate permanent BGP filtering to avoid short-lived re-advertisements, (2) revisit LB affinity as a configurable policy per-customer, (3) postmortem with partner.

incident-bot: Handoff logged: tj-oncall -> maya at 12:30 UTC. Monitoring channel created: #incidents-2337004000-monitoring.

maya: closing temporary actions doc and will update postmortem draft. Thanks all. :white_check_mark:
